title: Flying into Spain over buttermilk skies
summary: He describes the beauty of landing in Spain, the sea, whitecaps and the airfield beside the water.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah, they had some television, they -- well in Spain, I don't know why it came to my mind. Well, the first time we'd been in Spain, and oh, it was so pretty. The flying in, the skies looked like buttermilk. I mean they said buttermilk skies, and that's -- maybe that's what they meant, because we were so damn high up, and flying and everything was so quiet, and sun, everywhere you looked was sunshine. Everywhere! Everywhere!

Now as the plane starts to settling down, we're coming down over the sea there, and the water was so pretty and blue! And here and there you could see a ripple -- what you call them? The -- as the water would --
Yeah, you know, just enough white -- just enough --

And when they sat down, the airport is right on the side, and the whole thing looked like a beautiful pool table, and you set the plane down, and here's the airfield, and here's the water. It was so damn close I thought they were going to sit in the water there for a minute, you know?
Yeah -- no! It was so quiet, and so peaceful, and beautiful. I mean I was -- I'd never seen anything like that in my life. So --
